info.description:
# Alfa Commerce REST API

A Joomla JSON:API for Alfa Commerce. Every response is a JSON:API document: `data`, `links`, and `meta['total-pages']` on lists. The collection is generated from the published code (its route table, its controllers and its views) and carries a test on every request: run it with the Collection Runner or newman to check a shop's API route by route.

**Run it against a test or demo shop, never a live one.** It creates its own records and removes them, and its Orders and Documents folders place one order, issue its invoice on the shop's default invoice series (the shop needs one) and void it. Each full run leaves on record what the shop's rules keep: that order, cancelled, with its voided invoice (an issued document is immutable), its product, archived (a product with order history is not deleted), and, in the trash, the product's category and the payment and shipment methods the order used.

## Setup

Two collection variables, nothing else:

| Variable | Value |
|-|-|
| `baseUrl` | `https://your-shop.example/api/index.php` |
| `token` | your Joomla API token: **set this yourself** |

`token` ships empty on purpose: this collection lives in a shared workspace, and a token pasted here would be a live credential in a public document. Create one per user under **Users, Manage, edit user, Joomla API Token**, then paste it into the variable (or, better, an Environment).

Authentication is set once at collection level as the header `X-Joomla-Token: {{token}}`. `Authorization: Bearer <token>` works identically if you prefer it. A request without a token answers 401.

The requests keep the ids they create in collection variables of their own (`itemId`, `opsOrderId`, `documentId` and so on), so a folder runs top to bottom. The Customers folder uses Joomla core's own Users routes to make and remove a test user and group; the Documents and Tasks folders read what Orders, operations made, so run the collection in order.

## The two catalogue trees

The same product id answers differently depending on which tree you ask, and that is deliberate.

| | **Catalogue (storefront)** | **Catalogue (back office)** |
|-|-|-|
| Route | `v1/alfa/catalog/items` | `v1/alfa/items` |
| Served by | site models | administrator models |
| Visibility | published, inside the publish window, access allowed | every row |
| Unpublished product | `404` | `200` |
| Payload | resolved translations, computed price, variants, fields, media | raw editable row |
| Writes | none: read only | full CRUD |

Build storefronts and apps against the storefront tree; edit through the back office tree.

## Reading

- **Pagination**: `page[limit]` (default 20) and `page[offset]`. An offset past the end answers `404`.
- **Sorting**: `list[ordering]` and `list[direction]`. A column outside the model's whitelist is *silently ignored* rather than rejected, and an invalid direction becomes `asc`.
- **Filtering**: `filter[...]` per endpoint; see each List request. `filter[search]` also understands an `id:123` prefix for an exact match. The filters are the ones the back office's list screens offer and are applied the same way; a filter a list does not have is ignored, and one sent as a list (`filter[x][]=`) where one value is expected answers 400.
- **Language**: `?lang=el-GR` (or `el_gr`) selects the language translatable fields resolve in. An unknown or unpublished tag silently falls back to the site default, so read the `Content-Language` response header to see what you got. This is a *content* selector only; error messages stay in the API's own language.
- **Pricing context**: on the storefront tree, `?currency=` and `?place=` set the pricing dimensions. Without them prices use the shop default, which is wrong for a multi-currency shop rather than merely approximate.
- **Money**: an order's and a document's money is an object `{amount, formatted, minor_units}` with `amount` as exact decimal text; rates and stored figures are exact decimal text too ("24", "19.90").

## Writing

**A create answers 201 Created** with the new record and a `Location` header that names it.

**Multilingual fields.** Translatable text lives in per-language tables, never on the main row. Send either the flat per-language keys the admin form posts (`name_el_gr`, `name_en_gb`) or the nested map a GET returns:

```json
{ "translations": { "el-GR": { "name": "Νέο" }, "en-GB": { "name": "New" } } }
```

Both spellings of the tag work, and an explicit flat key wins over the nested map. **The key for the default language of a required field is mandatory on a create**: validation reads `<field>_<default_lang>` straight from the request. A PATCH that leaves a required name out keeps the stored names; one that sends it empty is refused (400).

**Relations are preserved, not replaced.** Omit `categories`, `manufacturers`, `allowedUsers`, `allowedUserGroups`, `prices` or `groups` and they are left exactly as they were. Send `[]` to clear one deliberately. A PATCH of one scalar can never quietly wipe a product's categories. An item's options, combinations, item field values and downloads, and an item field's `values`, are not written by the API (422 naming them).

**Media.** Send a declarative list; `medias` is accepted as an alias for `media`:

```json
{ "media": [ { "type": "image", "path": "images/x.jpg", "alt": "...", "ordering": 1 },
             { "type": "url",   "url": "https://cdn.example.com/y.jpg", "alt": "..." } ] }
```

Semantics are **merge**: a row you do not send stays, and removing one needs `"delete": 1`. Site-relative paths must already exist under a media root and are copied into the media zone. `type: "url"` accepts `http` and `https` only. An `alt` longer than 75 characters is refused (400). To upload new bytes, `POST` them to Joomla's own `v1/media/files` first and then reference the returned path.

**Long work: meta.tasks.** A save keeps its own status and still says what it left to the shop's background work: the answer's `meta.tasks` lists the jobs the request queued or joined (and, on an order, the singles it wrote), each with its state and a self link under `v1/alfa/tasks`. See the Tasks folder.

## Deleting, and the answers that refuse

- A successful delete answers **204** with no body.
- A product, a category, a manufacturer, an item field, a currency, a tax, a discount, a place, a payment or shipping method, a form field, a form field group or an order status is deleted only while it is in the trash (`state: -2`), as the back office deletes it: a DELETE of one in any other state answers **409** with the reason and deletes nothing; a PATCH of `state: -2` trashes it first. Cart rules, stock locations, customers, customer groups and orders are deleted in one call, as the back office deletes them; a cart rule and an order have no trash step over the API.
- A product that order lines were sold as is archived instead of deleted: its DELETE answers **200** with the product, archived (`state: 2`), and `meta.note` saying why.
- A delete the model refuses by its own rule (a category that still has children or is a product's default, an entity whose delete would widen a discount, tax or cart rule, an order with sales documents, an order whose payment or shipping plugin of record cannot be asked, an order status orders are in, a payment or shipping method, a currency or an item field still in use) answers **409** with the refusal's sentence.
- An id that names no record answers **404**; so does the delete of an order already deleted.
- The order operations answer **409** for a refused business rule (a refund through the payments route, a settle whose `from_status` does not match, a cancelled order reinstated without `force`) and **422** where the ledger refuses (a refund of a payment that is not completed, an unknown status), each with its sentence; **400** for input that is not usable (an amount finer than the order's currency, a JSON number that does not carry its digits exactly: send money as a string).
- `PATCH v1/alfa/orders/:id` never writes `id_order_status` or `state` (**422**): `POST v1/alfa/orders/:id/status` is the one status entry point. It writes an order's `customer_note` and its delivery and invoice details (`alfa_form_fields`, `alfa_form_fields_billing` with `invoice_differs`); any other field the order publishes answers **422** naming it, and nothing is saved, `id_address_delivery` and `created` among them.

## Permissions

Every route is gated on the `alfa.<entity>.<action>` permissions from the component's Options, Permissions (the order operations on the orders edit permission; the status change on Change State and view; a void on the documents Change State). Nothing Joomla's core rights grant counts: a Super User passes, everyone else needs what a Super User granted. A token whose user lacks the permission gets `403`, not an empty list.

## Renamed and removed endpoints

- `v1/alfa/payments` and `v1/alfa/shipments` are now `v1/alfa/paymentmethods` and `v1/alfa/shipmentmethods` (a payment or shipment METHOD is configuration); the old names answer 404. An order's own payments and shipments are `v1/alfa/orders/:id/payments` and `v1/alfa/orders/:id/shipments`.
- `itemsprices`, `customs`, `coupons` and `settings` were removed: item prices are part of the item payload, custom fields became **item fields**, coupons became **cart rules**, and component settings are Joomla core's `v1/config/com_alfa`.

## Behaviour worth knowing

- A create answers 201 Created with a `Location` header.
- A delete the model refuses answers 409 with the reason: an order status orders are in, a payment or shipping method, a currency or an item field still in use.
- A tax, discount or cart rule that does not exist answers 404.
- Without the dompdf library (lib_dompdf), a document's PDF answers 503 with a sentence that names the library.
- A PATCH keeps what it leaves out: a required name, and the price display flags of a customer group it does not name.
- A PATCH of an order's `state` answers 422 with the reason; `customer_note` is written.
- A single order carries `fulfillment_status` and `fulfillment_percentage`; a payment carries `added` and `refund_reason`.
- List filters, applied as the back office's lists apply them: orders by `payment`, `fulfilment`, `waiting`, `reconciliation`, `overpaid`, `date_start`, `date_end`, `item_id`, and by customer (`id_user`, 0 for the guests' orders; `email`); movements by `date_start`, `date_end` and `item_id`; documents by `date_start` and `date_end`; items by `stock` and `fields`. An empty value is no filter; an end date with no time is that whole day.
- A POST or PATCH of an item that carries `fields`, `options`, `combinations` or `informational` (or the edit form's keys for them, `item_downloads` among them) answers 422 naming them. A POST or PATCH of an item field that carries `values` or `deleted_value_ids` answers 422 the same way.
- An order's payments and shipments are read through `GET v1/alfa/orders/:id`: there are no GET routes for them.
- A record of the resources the back office deletes only from its trash is deleted only while it is in the trash: a DELETE of one in any other state answers 409.
- A DELETE of a product with order history answers 200 with the product, archived, and `meta.note`.
- A PATCH of an order that carries a field its update does not write answers 422 naming it. `id_address_delivery` and `created` are refused too.
- Each entry of an order's `shipments` carries `added`, `shipping_charge_basis` and `shipping_tax_chain`.
- `silent` on a status change leaves out the customer's e-mail only; the staff the status tells still receive theirs.
